name: Pea Soup
lede: Pea Soup is a murky, yellow-leaning [[green]], named directly for the thick split-pea soup it resembles rather than for fresh peas.

sections.title: The soup, not the vegetable
sections.body:
Our graph files this as a food-and-landscape name rather than a modifier, recorded by the xkcd 2010 crowd survey [1]. The ISCC-NBS system places the family as "deep greenish yellow", block 100, about 3.7 units from this exact swatch [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[baby-shit-green]], [[vomit]] and [[pea-soup-green]], at 2.9, 
The color is murkier than most greens: the same murk gave English the idiom "pea-souper" for a thick yellow-brown fog, a usage this swatch echoes more than a bowl of fresh green peas does [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Pea Soup appears in 14 of our 23,781 paintings by raw coverage, and in 12 of those by its position in the painting's lightness order, as photographed [2]. That makes it rarer than 66% of the named colors we track [2].

It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, found in 0.4% of our 1,674 paintings from that decade, 4.1 times the archive's baseline rate [2]. Where it appears, it most often sits as an accent, the role in 67% of its 12 matched paintings [2]. The earliest match is 1775 (cma-169253), 235 years before the name's own 2010 record, so it is a look-alike hue, not evidence the color was named or mixed that way at the time, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
